jobs.title: Specialista in Ginecologia e Ostetricia – 100%
jobs.description_text:
Descrizione dell'azienda
Centromedico è una realtà sanitaria consolidata in Ticino, nata con l’obiettivo di offrire un modello di cura moderno, accessibile e centrato sul paziente. Nel corso degli anni ha sviluppato un approccio multidisciplinare che riunisce medici di base, specialisti e servizi diagnostici sotto un unico tetto, garantendo qualità, continuità e tempi di attesa ridotti. L’attenzione alla professionalità del team e all’accoglienza del paziente rappresenta da sempre uno dei pilastri del suo successo.
Grazie alla presenza capillare delle sue sedi, collocate strategicamente sul territorio ticinese, Centromedico offre un servizio di prossimità esteso a tutto il Cantone. Questa distribuzione consente ai pazienti di accedere facilmente alle cure, vicino a casa o al luogo di lavoro, mantenendo standard omogenei di qualità e un’esperienza di cura semplice, chiara e personalizzata.
Descrizione del lavoro
Per il nostro centro medico di Locarno siamo alla ricerca di un/a Medico/a specialista in Ginecologia e Ostetricia, con grado di occupazione al 100%, interessato/a a entrare a far parte di una realtà sanitaria strutturata e multidisciplinare.
La figura selezionata svolgerà attività specialistica ambulatoriale in autonomia, occupandosi della presa a carico delle pazienti nell'ambito della prevenzione, diagnosi, trattamento e follow-up delle principali patologie ginecologiche.
Principali attività
Visite ginecologiche e controlli specialistici
Attività di prevenzione e screening
Diagnosi, trattamento e follow-up delle patologie ginecologiche
Consulenza e accompagnamento delle pazienti nelle diverse fasi della vita
Collaborazione con i medici e gli altri professionisti sanitari presenti all'interno della struttura
Gestione autonoma dell'attività ambulatoriale, con il supporto del personale del centro
Qualifiche
Titolo di Medico specialista in Ginecologia e Ostetricia riconosciuto in Svizzera o riconoscibile tramite MEBEKO
Requisiti necessari per l'esercizio della professione medica in Canton Ticino
Ottima conoscenza della lingua italiana (la conoscenza del tedesco costituisce carattere preferenziale)
Autonomia professionale e capacità organizzative
Attitudine al lavoro interdisciplinare
Approccio professionale, empatico e orientato alla qualità della presa a carico del paziente
Ulteriori informazioni
Inserimento in una realtà strutturata e in crescita
Team multidisciplinare qualificato
Condizioni contrattuali attrattive
Opportunità di sviluppo professionale e formazione continua

Reparto: Centromedico SMN SA
Tasso di occupazione: 100 %
Data di inizio: Da subito o da convenire

jobs.title: Financial Accountant
jobs.description_text:
Company Description
Arista Networks is an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large data center, campus and routing environments. What sets us apart is our relentless pursuit of innovation. We leverage the latest advancements in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and software-defined networking to provide our clients with a competitive edge in an increasingly interconnected world. Our solutions are designed to not only meet the current demands of the digital landscape but to also anticipate and adapt to future challenges.
At Arista we value the diversity of thought and perspectives that each employee brings to the table. We believe that fostering an inclusive environment, where individuals from various backgrounds and experiences feel welcome, is essential for driving creativity and innovation.
Our commitment to excellence has earned us several prestigious awards, such as Best Engineering Team, Best Company for Diversity, Compensation, and Work-Life Balance. At Arista, we take pride in our track record of success and strive to maintain the highest standards of quality and performance in everything we do.
Job Description
Who You'll Work For
Arista is looking for a Financial Accountant to join its finance team in Shannon on an 18-month contract. This is an established role with a well-defined remit: you'll own the day-to-day accounting, month-end close and statutory reporting for six of Arista's international legal entities, working closely with the corporate accounting, international tax, treasury, payroll, accounts payable and accounts receivable teams.
Beyond the day-to-day, you will have scope to improve processes and controls, and you will gain hands-on exposure to US GAAP reporting, SOX controls and Irish/EMEA statutory compliance within a fast-growing, NYSE-listed global technology company.
What You'll Do
Lead the monthly and quarterly close for six international entities, meeting group reporting deadlines.
General ledger responsibility for prepaid expenses, fixed assets, accrued expenses, bank, other assets and liabilities, along with intercompany and payroll transactions.
Prepare and review journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations.
Manage the annual statutory audits for the entities, including preparation of the financial statements and directors’ reports in accordance with the local GAAP of each region.
Prepare and submit monthly and quarterly CSO statistical surveys.
Operate and improve SOX controls within your area and help maintain finance policies and procedures.
Manage external service providers, such as auditors and local advisors, and build strong working relationships with stakeholders across Arista.
Partner with the Marketing team on billing event sponsorship contributions to partners across all subsidiaries.
Maintain clear process documentation and support cross-training so that team coverage is resilient.
Identify and deliver process improvements that increase efficiency and accuracy.
Other projects/duties as required.
#LI-EO1
Qualifications
Qualified chartered accountant with 2+ years’ post qualification experience, ideally in a multinational or listed company.
Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and FRS102, and of Irish and EMEA statutory reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience of month-end close, balance sheet reconciliations and statutory audits.
Experience working in a SOX-controlled environment.
Advanced Excel skills.
Proactive approach to identifying and implementing AI solutions to automate routine financial workflows and drive operational efficiency.
Strong organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing deadlines.
A clear communicator who works well both independently and as part of a team.
Desirable
Experience using NetSuite.
Inter company accounting experience across multiple jurisdictions.
Experience in the technology sector.
Additional Information
Contract: 18-month contract.
Location: Shannon, Co. Clare. Hybrid working, with more time on-site during the initial onboarding period and greater flexibility once you are settled into the role.
Hours: Due to the international nature of this role a degree of flexibility will be offered and will be required in relation to the working hours.
Rate: Competitive, depending on experience. Full contract terms will be discussed at interview.
What’s on Offer
Hybrid working
Flexitime
On-site parking
Company events
Wellness programme

jobs.title: People & Development Assistant
jobs.description_text:
Company Description
Portaluna, a Morgans Originals Hotel
Morgans Originals are original hotels with original stories. We stand for vibrancy, intrigue and iconic details, celebrating the feeling of an infinite Friday night, when anything can happen, no matter what day of the week it is. By balancing a refined outlook with the best lifestyle programming, we capture the excitement of being in-the-know -- connecting people to the city, the culture and the moment.
This is an exciting new position within Ennismore’s growing portfolio of lifestyle brands, representing the first Morgans Originals hotel in Egypt.
Job Description
About the Role
We are looking for a passionate, highly organized, and detail-oriented People & Development Assistant to join our HR team. In this role, you will play a key part in supporting the full employee lifecycle—from talent acquisition and onboarding to supporting learning and development programs and fostering a positive, engaging workplace culture.
Key Responsibilities
Talent Acquisition Support: Assist in drafting and posting job descriptions, screening resumes, coordinating interview schedules, and communicating with candidates.
Employee Onboarding: Prepare welcome packages, coordinate contract signing, and manage the orientation process for new hires to ensure a seamless integration into the company.
HR Administration & Records: Maintain and update employee databases and digital personnel files accurately and confidentially; track employment contracts and renewals.
Learning & Development Support: Assist in coordinating training sessions, booking venues or virtual platforms, evaluating training effectiveness, and tracking employee attendance.
Day-to-Day Operations: Serve as a first point of contact for employee inquiries regarding internal policies and procedures, and handle general administrative tasks for the HR team.
Employee Engagement & Culture: Contribute to organizing company events, team-building activities, and initiatives focused on improving workplace environment and employee satisfaction.
Requirements & Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field.
Experience: 0–2 years of experience in Human Resources (previous HR internships are a strong plus).
Soft Skills:
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with strong interpersonal abilities.
Strong organizational skills, the ability to multitask, and a keen eye for detail.
High level of professional integrity and discretion when handling confidential information.
Technical Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and familiarity with Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS).
Languages: Full professional proficiency in both Arabic and English (spoken and written).
What We Offer
A supportive, dynamic work environment that encourages continuous learning and professional growth.
Competitive salary and benefits package (commensurate with qualifications and experience).
Genuine opportunities for career advancement within the People & Development department.

Additional Information
What awaits you...
The opportunity to join an international and innovative and fast-growing group, committed not only to building new hotels, but to creating a global brand.
The ability to challenge the norm and work in an environment that is both creative and rewarding.
Be part of a team that is very passionate about creating great hospitality experiences and exploring new locations with every opportunity.
A competitive package and plenty of development opportunities.

jobs.title: Store Clerk
jobs.description_text:
Our ideal candidate would have a positive attitude, be someone who is hard working, available and be open to advancement opportunities.  

Cooperative Producers, Inc. (CPI) offers a diverse range of employment opportunities that span a wide variety of fields. We continuously seek enthusiastic and qualified individuals who can help contribute to the growth and success of our cooperative.

CPI is seeking a dedicated Store Clerk to join our expanding team. We deeply value our employees' contributions and are committed to their professional development, engagement, and success. We recruit and retain the best people to continually deliver exceptional value.

CPI is proudly committed to our "Making Local Matter" initiative by forging enduring partnerships with local farmers and actively supporting the communities of Northern Kansas and Central Nebraska. As an employee of CPI, you will have the opportunity to make a positive impact on your community and support CPI's mission of making local matter.

What the job is:

CPI is looking for someone with experience preferably in a convenient store or retail setting who knows how to work hard, greet customers with a smile, count change back and maintain a retail store setting.  The ideal candidate will have previous experience stocking shelves, creating displays, preparing food service items and receiving payments for products sold.   CPI is a safety minded company thus such policies must be followed.  Store Clerks will also complete daily housekeeping to assure the safety for all persons entering the store, monitor customer transactions and experiences and follow proper guidelines as established by CPI.  

•    High School Diploma or GED or related experience and/or training in retail. 

•    May be required to lift up to 10 pounds at a time.  

•    Prolonged periods of standing, walking and working at a cash register.  

•    Occasionally required to sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl.  

•    Generous benefits and competitive wages. Premium pay for qualified bilingual candidates.

Please inquire within for full job description.

CPI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment.

jobs.title: Process Operator
jobs.description_text:
Reporting to: Team Manager
Reference: R9975

Summary
The Process Operator reports directly to the Team Manager and the Production Manager in the Team Managers absence ensuring the mill runs at optimized efficiency whilst maintaining the company quality standards and UFAS requirements. 

They ensure that a high level of Health & Safety and Hygiene is always adhered to throughout the mill and that the production plan is on time to the targeted efficiency whilst maintaining high quality of product. 

Additional responsibilities will include warehouse duties and when required FLT duties and other duties within reasonable request , in a safe and legal manner and to the correct quality standards and UFAS requirements, assist and support Engineers, Team Managers and Shift Technicians during breakdowns and planned maintenance. 
Role and Responsibilities
Communicate to Colleagues and other departments if there are any issues is achieving the plan
Ensure Environmental management system is followed and adhered to complying with BS EN ISO 14001/50001
Ensure their shift is maintained to high level of H&S , and any issues are communicated in a timely manner and actions completed
Maintain site processes/standard in line with the UFAS code of practice
To ensure that the working area is maintained to an acceptable standard of Hygiene throughout shift
Run the intake/grinding/blending/pelleting/packing and loading processes in an efficient manner to deliver the production plan on time
Communicate all issue/delays against the plan to colleagues and other departments
Proactively reduce any areas that actively are generating waste
Maintain the routine machine maintenance and cleaning schedules
Optimise utilisation of finished product bin space
Cover all process roles during holidays and/or any other form of absence
Support the team with all processes and additional tasks.
Deputise for the Supervisor when required

Skills and Experience
Team Player
Good attitude
Self-Motivated
Good communicator
Proactively/forward thinker
Feed mill Experience required
Supervisory experience in a manufacturing environment preferred
Ability to communicate at different levels
FLT Driver
Experience of process control systems
A good understanding of Office software

Applications
We value diversity in our workplace and welcome enquiries from everyone.

Candidates wishing to apply who would require sponsorship can determine the likelihood of obtaining a Certificate of Sponsorship for the role by assessing their circumstances against the relevant criteria on the Gov.UK website.

Please make us aware if your need any reasonable adjustments to participate in this process.

We encourage you to submit your application as early as possible and not wait as closing dates may vary.
